title: Protocols for analyzing metabolic derangements caused by increased NADH/NAD+ ratio in cell lines and in mice
protocol: Culture 143B cells in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin and 2 mM L-glutamine.
Seed 3 million 143B cells onto a 6-cm dish and culture for 16 h.
Aspirate medium from cells.
Add fresh medium containing DMSO or ETC inhibitors (piericidin A: 10 μM; antimycin A, 10 μM) in the presence or absence of NAD+ regeneration supplementations (3 mM pyruvate or 3 mM α-ketobutyrate).
Incubate cells for 2 h.
Wash cells with PBS twice quickly.
Add 4 mL deuterium-glucose (10 mM) tracing medium supplemented with same inhibitors and incubate for the indicated time (12 h for [4-2H]-glucose, 4 h for [3-2H]-glucose).
Wash cells with PBS twice quickly.
Aspirate PBS from dishes.
Add 1 mL ice-cold acetonitrile/methanol/water (4/4/2) containing 0.1 M formic acid to the dishes on ice.
Incubate cells on ice for 2 min.
Add 87 μL 15% ammonium bicarbonate to neutralize samples.
Mix immediately after addition.
Quickly wash cells with PBS twice.
Incubate cells with [U-13C]-glucose (10mM) tracing medium supplemented with inhibitors for 5 minutes, starting a timer when incubation begins.
After 4 minutes and 20 seconds of incubation, quickly aspirate the medium and wash cells with PBS twice.
Aspirate PBS and add 1 mL of −80°C pre-chilled 80% methanol immediately when the timer reaches 5 minutes.
Put the dish on dry ice immediately after adding methanol.
Scrape cells on ice to collect cell lysates in a tube.
Vortex the cell lysate at 4°C for 1 minute.
Centrifuge the cell lysate at 20,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully transfer the supernatants to a new tube and keep the pellets.
Dry the supernatants by a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator at 4°C.
Store dried samples at -80°C.
Dissolve cell pellets in 600 μL 0.1 M KOH by shaking on a tube rotator at 4°C for 10–16 h.
Measure protein concentration using the Bradford assay kit.
Maintain C57BL/6J mice at 6-8 weeks old under a 12-h light/dark cycle and on a standard chow diet in an SPF facility.
Gently restrain the mouse by grasping the loose skin of the neck and back to immobilize the head for oral gavage.
Restrain the mouse with the left hand by grasping the loose skin over the shoulders and behind the ears.
Puncture the vein with a 25 gauge needle slightly behind the mandible, but in front of the ear canal.
Collect about 350 μl blood into the blood collection tube held by another person.
Place the blood sample on ice.
Sacrifice the mice immediately after blood collection.
Dissect out the liver and immediately place it into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Freeze the liver in liquid nitrogen within seconds.
Store frozen tissues at -80°C.
Extract plasma metabolites immediately after blood collection.
Centrifuge blood samples at 1,500 g for 10 min at 4°C.
After centrifugation, if red blood cells are intact during blood collection, the upper plasma fraction is nearly colorless.
If red blood cells are ruptured during blood collection, the upper plasma fraction is pink or red.
During centrifugation, prepare a new Eppendorf tube with 1 mL extraction buffer on ice for each sample.
Carefully transfer 50 μL upper plasma fraction into the prepared extraction buffer.
Mix the extraction buffer and the plasma sample immediately by up and down shaking.
Vortex all samples on a microtube holder for 1 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge samples at 20,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to a new tube carefully without perturbing the pellets.
Dry the supernatants by a SpeedVac vacuum concentrator at 4°C.
Store dried samples at -80°C before mass-spec analysis.
Analyze the samples within 24 hours to avoid metabolites degradation.
Put −80°C frozen tissues into liquid nitrogen.
Grind the tissue in a mixer mill MM400 at liquid nitrogen temperature.
Prechill the rack in a liquid nitrogen bath.
Put the tissue containing tubes into the rack and run at 30 frequency/s for 30 s.
Place the tissue containing tubes into liquid nitrogen before weighing.
Weigh approximately 30 mg of tissues into a pre-cooled homogenizing tube with 12 zirconia grinding beads.
Seal the tube and place it into liquid nitrogen.
Put the tubes on ice after weighing all the tissue samples.
Add approximately 600 μL ice-cold acetonitrile/methanol/water (4/4/2) to the tubes at a ratio of 20 μL/mg tissue.
Homogenize the tissue for 1 min at 6.5 m/s at 4°C in the tissue homogenizer.
Place the tubes on ice for 2 min after initial homogenization.
Repeat the homogenization process and cooling.
Centrifuge the samples at 20,000 g for 1 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatants into new Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the samples again at 20,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatants to new Eppendorf tubes after centrifugation.
Dry the supernatants using a Speedvac vacuum concentrator at 4°C.
Store dried samples at -80°C before mass-spec analysis.
Prepare a stock solution of metabolite standards at 1 mg/mL with ultrapure water.
If necessary, sonicate the compound at 25°C for 20 minutes to ensure full dissolution.
Take 10 μL from each 1 mg/mL stock solution of metabolite standard and add to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 50% MeOH to make the final volume in the tube 1 mL.
Split the 1 mL 10 μg/mL mixed standard solution into 10 aliquots of 100 μL each.
Store the 100 μL aliquots at -80°C.
Take one aliquot of mixed standard solution on the day of experiment.
Run biological samples parallelly with the standard solution.
Put dried samples stored at −80°C on ice.
Add 100 μL 50% methanol to the samples and vortex for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the samples at 20,000 g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Filter the supernatants through 0.45 μm filters.
Transfer filtered supernatants to HPLC glass vials with micro-inserts.
Screw the cap on the HPLC glass vials.
Analyze biological samples using a high-resolution LC-MS system, such as Vanquish UHPLC - Q Exactive HF-X Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap MS.
Identify the retention time of the target metabolite in the metabolite standard sample.
Use a retention time window of 0.1 min as reference to identify metabolites and record peak heights.
Check carefully that all metabolites have a retention time window less than 0.1 min.
Normalize peak heights to protein concentration.
Calculate the mass isotopomer distribution of each metabolite after natural abundance correction using IsoCor software.
